1. Lecture Scope & Why Finite Fourier Transforms?

Reading: Deen 5.3–5.8.

Learning objective: develop methods to solve different classes of two- (or more-) dimensional problems in fluid mechanics.

The original Handout 09 places this lecture inside a broader sequence of solution methods:

  1. Separation of variables / finite Fourier transforms.
  2. Combination of variables.
  3. Lubrication approximation.
  4. Boundary layer theory.
  5. Stream functions.

Handout 09 presents the finite Fourier transform method as a generalization of the separation-of-variables method from Handout 08. The lecture emphasizes that separation of variables can become cumbersome for some boundary conditions, whereas a finite Fourier transform can provide a more flexible route while using the same orthogonality ideas.

The method is demonstrated first on a problem already solved by separation of variables. After the machinery is established, the lecture applies it to a more general two-dimensional boundary-value problem.

Remember. The transform does not “solve the PDE by magic.” It removes one coordinate by projecting the PDE onto an orthonormal basis. The remaining unknown coefficient satisfies an ODE in the remaining variable.
دیدگاه درست این است که تبدیل فوریهٔ محدود یک روش حذف متغیر است. با ضرب کردن معادله در تابع پایه و انتگرال‌گیری روی بازهٔ محدود، وابستگی به یک مختصات حذف می‌شود و مسئله به معادله‌ای ساده‌تر برای ضریب هر مد تبدیل می‌شود.

6.6 Physical meaning of a source term

The original slide frames the as a constant heating source. In the in-class annotations, the momentum-transport analogy is “injecting momentum: fan,” and the mass-transport analogy is “injecting mass: add liquid.” The mathematical role is the same: the source contributes an additional nonhomogeneous term after transformation.

7. Common Problem-Solving Pattern

  1. Write the PDE and every boundary/initial condition. Keep the coordinate interval explicit.
  2. Choose the transform coordinate. Prefer the direction whose boundary conditions can be matched by a simple orthonormal basis.
  3. Select the basis function. Check its value or derivative at both boundaries and record the correct index range.
  4. Write the series form and define the transform .
  5. Transform the PDE term-by-term. Move derivatives in the transformed coordinate onto the basis using integration by parts—twice for a second derivative.
  6. Apply boundary conditions immediately to eliminate boundary terms from integration by parts.
  7. Use the eigenfunction relation such as to rewrite the integral in terms of .
  8. Transform source terms, initial conditions, and the remaining boundary conditions. These become forcing terms or conditions for the transformed ODE.
  9. Solve the ODE for each mode. Choose exponentials or hyperbolic functions according to convenience.
  10. Reconstruct the original field by substituting back into the series.
برای حل سریع مسئله، ترتیب مراحل را ثابت نگه دارید. ابتدا شرط‌های مرزی و جهت تبدیل را مشخص کنید، سپس پایه را انتخاب کنید، بعد تبدیل را روی تک‌تک جمله‌های معادله انجام دهید. اگر این ترتیب به هم بخورد، معمولاً علامت‌ها، شرط‌های مرزی یا ضرایب نرمال‌سازی اشتباه می‌شوند.

9. Key Assumptions & Boundary Conditions

Method structure

  • The coordinate being transformed lies on a finite interval, consistent with the finite-Fourier-transform setup used in Handout 09.
  • A basis is selected that is orthonormal on that interval.
  • The chosen basis is tailored to the boundary conditions so that boundary terms simplify.
  • After transformation, the PDE becomes an ODE in the remaining variable.

Transient example

  • Sine basis,

Laplace example

  • Homogeneous value conditions at
  • Specified functions at
  • Transform in

In-class source example

  • Constant source

10. Common Mistakes

  • Choosing a basis before reading both boundary conditions. The basis must match the value/derivative condition at each end.
  • Forgetting the normalization factor . Then is no longer equal to the transform coefficient under the stated convention.
  • Integrating by parts only once. A second spatial derivative requires two passes to place the second derivative on .
  • Losing the minus sign in .
  • Using the wrong mode indexing. Sine Case I starts at ; the half-integer cosine Case II starts at .
  • Not transforming the source term. The transform of the constant source is , not simply 1.
  • Forgetting to transform the remaining boundary or initial conditions. The ODE is not complete without them.
  • Confusing , , and the full . Keep basis, modal coefficient, and reconstructed field distinct.
  • Assuming cosine means derivative-zero at both boundaries. The half-integer cosine used in class has derivative-zero at one boundary and value-zero at the other.
رایج‌ترین خطا این است که تابع پایه درست انتخاب نشود یا شرط‌های مرزی پس از تبدیل فراموش شوند. هر بار قبل از شروع انتگرال‌گیری، مقدار خود تابع پایه و مشتق آن را در دو مرز بنویسید. این بررسی کوتاه جلوی بیشتر خطاهای علامت و مرز را می‌گیرد.

11. What I Need to Know for the Exam

Course note from the in-class sheet. The handwritten page notes “expand in Cartesian coordinates” and describes the exam as two longer problems during the class period with extra time. Treat these as notes from that class session rather than a replacement for any later course announcement.

Core skills to be able to do without notes

  1. Recognize when a finite Fourier transform is a natural extension of separation of variables.
  2. Choose the transform direction from the boundary conditions.
  3. Select the correct sine/cosine basis and the correct index range.
  4. Write the transform definition and series expansion.
  5. Transform a second derivative by integrating by parts twice and explain why each boundary term vanishes.
  6. Use to obtain the transformed ODE.
  7. Transform initial conditions, boundary conditions, and source terms.
  8. Solve the resulting first- or second-order ODE, including a nonhomogeneous ODE with a constant particular solution.
  9. Reconstruct the full series solution and keep the modal coefficient distinct from the basis function.
Fast self-check. Before you commit to a basis, verify its value and derivative at both boundaries. Before you solve the transformed ODE, verify that you transformed every PDE term and every condition. Before you reconstruct, verify the mode indexing and normalization.
برای امتحان باید بتوانید از روی صورت مسئله تشخیص دهید کدام جهت را تبدیل کنید و کدام پایه را انتخاب کنید. مهم‌تر از حفظ جواب نهایی، توانایی اجرای فرایند است: تبدیل جمله‌به‌جمله، دو بار جزءبه‌جزء کردن، تبدیل شرط‌ها، حل معادلهٔ معمولی و بازسازی سری.
